title: IFT-12 — Starship V3 Debut
description: 22 May 2026. First flight of Starship V3 (S39 / B19). One Raptor fails on ship — autonomous guidance extends burn 62 s to compensate. Booster lost in Gulf after boostback anomaly. Ship splashes down in Indian Ocean.
author: Markus Leutwyler

engineFailures._note: Raptor 5 on ship shuts down ~6 s after sep ignition; guidance extends burn autonomously

atcClearances.text: All right, all operators on countdown one.
Flight directors go for launch.
We have set you downrange.
Opter chamber pressure nominal.
33 out of 33 Raptor 3 engines on booster V3, ascending over the Gulf now.
Booster and ship avionics power telemetry nominal.
Successful hot staging separation. We are not seeing as many booster engines ignite as we expected for boostback.
It looks like we just had an early boostback shutdown.
Arvacs have shut down. Sea levels have shut down. Ship FTS is saved.
Awaiting the callout of nominal insertion.
Within bounds of what we analyzed. It's on a trajectory now headed towards the other side of the planet.
PEZ door is open. Pew pew. Two down, 20 to go.
Starship, basically serving the first Dodger dogs to low Earth orbit.
Let there be light.
Engine chill has started.
Entry max heating. Entry max Q.
Ship has passed through the peak heating region. External temperatures are coming down.
Ship flap load test has started.
Test is complete.
Starship is starting the RTLS banking maneuver.
Starship is subsonic and is on target.
Landing burn start up.
Two engine flip.
Successful flip.
On target landing.

narrative: One Raptor fails on Ship — guidance extends burn 62 seconds.
debrief: Did the engine failure callout come at T+2:30?
Did the ship reach SECO despite flying on 5 engines?
How much longer did the burn last compared to a nominal 6-engine flight?
What happened to Booster 19 in the Gulf?
